title: MATCH and VLOOKUP require equal UTF-16 length in non-wildcard exact mode and count wildcard ? in UTF-16 units
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, MATCH(..., 0) and VLOOKUP(..., FALSE) without wildcards match only text of the same UTF-16 code-unit length: "SS" does not match "ß" and "ae" does not match "æ", whereas "e"&UNICHAR(769) (length 2) matches "e"+U+0301 in D2 rather than precomposed "é" in D1. In wildcard mode, "?" matches one UTF-16 code unit, so surrogate-pair emoji "😀" matches "??" rather than "?". Both functions read a blank or omitted lookup_value as 0 and reject lookup strings longer than 255 UTF-16 code units with #VALUE!.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in dczsn1_collation (rows 107-116) and fn1_collation (rows 217, 219), and matched across 3,373/3,373 MATCH and 3,680/3,680 VLOOKUP full-bank rows plus 13/13 MATCH pinned rows.
